scope.quote: All submissions must primarily be about R packages and R programming.

rules.quote: with the abstract no more than 250 words.
benefit beyond the specific application.
rules.requirement: For an application article, show value beyond the specific use case.

rules.quote: Articles for the R Journal should be no more than 20 pages
rules.requirement: Keep the article at or below 20 pages.

rules.quote: your references need to be contained in a .bib file.
rules.requirement: Put references in a .bib file.

rules.quote: Your submitted bib file should contain only the references actually cited in your paper.
rules.requirement: Include only cited references in the submitted .bib file.

rules.quote: Please also check that all references fields are properly formatted.
rules.requirement: Check the formatting of bibliography fields.

rules.quote: all code and data must be made available (publicly if we publish your submission).
rules.requirement: Make all code and data available, with public availability if published.

rules.quote: of implementations in base-R and contributed packages with each other
rules.requirement: For a comparison article, compare relevant base R or contributed package implementations.

rules.quote: explain the motivation for their contribution;
rules.requirement: Explain the motivation for the contribution.

rules.quote: Articles must not be published or submitted for publication elsewhere.
rules.requirement: Do not submit a previously published or concurrently submitted article.

rules.quote: the other software is open source and free to use
rules.requirement: If R calls other software, justify its use and ensure it meets the journal's openness and use conditions.

rules.quote: Figures and tables should have alt-text in chunk specifications, to assist with accessibility.
rules.requirement: Add alt text for figures and tables in source chunk specifications.

rules.quote: Each user-facing function must be fully documented with all terms and arguments explained, and examples provided.
rules.requirement: Document each user-facing function, its terms and arguments, and examples.

rules.quote: Ensure that R outputs are from an evaluation of R code rather than manually entering the outputs in the Rmd file.
rules.requirement: Generate R outputs by evaluating code in the R Markdown source.

rules.quote: If you do use LaTeX, you must use the LaTeX template.
rules.requirement: If submitting LaTeX source, use the journal LaTeX template.

rules.quote: are all the data files (if any) in an open, non-proprietary format?
rules.requirement: Provide any data files in an open, nonproprietary format.

rules.quote: is all code used open source and available via CRAN or Bioconductor?
rules.requirement: Use open-source code available through CRAN or Bioconductor for technical review.

rules.quote: Avoid unnecessary dependencies.
rules.requirement: Avoid unnecessary package dependencies.

rules.quote: The package is actively maintained and sufficiently mature.
rules.requirement: Provide evidence that the package is maintained and mature.

rules.quote: The package must include unit tests that verify output values, not merely output class or structure.
rules.requirement: Include package unit tests that check output values. Check package code, not only the article.

rules.quote: The package must be available on CRAN or Bioconductor.
rules.requirement: A package described by the article must be available on CRAN or Bioconductor.

rules.quote: The content of the package should be substantial and would likely be of significant interest and use within the R community.
rules.requirement: Show substantive package functionality and likely broad interest in the R community.

rules.quote: clearly demonstrate the use of the package and its advantages over any competing packages or existing approaches.
rules.requirement: Demonstrate package use and explain advantages over alternatives.

rules.quote: Include a vignette describing a full workflow or example analysis.
rules.requirement: Provide a package vignette with a full workflow or example analysis.

rules.quote: Papers must be fully reproducible
rules.requirement: Make results in the paper reproducible.

rules.quote: Titles and abstract should be in plain text
rules.requirement: Use plain text for title and abstract.

rules.quote: All submissions must primarily be about R packages and R programming.
rules.requirement: Keep the article primarily about R packages or R programming.

rules.quote: put their contribution in context, in particular discuss related R functions or packages;
rules.requirement: Discuss related R functions or packages to place the contribution in context.

rules.quote: If a submission cannot be reproduced in a reasonable time (less than 10 minutes), it will be sent back to you.
rules.requirement: Keep the submission reproducible within about ten minutes, or provide intermediate outputs for intensive methods.

rules.quote: you will need to enter the identifier of the original submission in the last field of the submission form.
rules.requirement: For revisions or resubmissions, enter the original submission identifier.

rules.quote: surveying and discussing challenges and opportunities of potential importance for the broader R community
rules.requirement: For a review or proposal, discuss challenges or opportunities relevant to the broader R community.

rules.quote: Please use rjtools instead of rticles.
rules.requirement: Use the rjtools template rather than the deprecated rticles format when writing in R Markdown.

rules.quote: The R Journal is primarily a software journal.
rules.requirement: Focus a package article on the software and its design rather than extensive method exposition.

rules.quote: Files to build the article.
rules.requirement: Include all source files needed to build the article.

rules.quote: A motivating letter that describes why your paper is suitable for consideration by the R Journal.
rules.requirement: Include a letter explaining suitability for The R Journal.

rules.quote: A list of R packages needed to reproduce the submission.
rules.requirement: Include a list of required R packages.

rules.quote: The article in .pdf format.
rules.requirement: Include a PDF of the article in the submission archive.

rules.quote: Files to reproduce the results, including R scripts, and data.
rules.requirement: Include R scripts and data needed to reproduce results.

rules.quote: Your files will need to be uploaded in a zip file that should contain:
rules.requirement: Upload the submission files as a ZIP archive.

rules.quote: Use a version control system (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, BitBucket, R-Forge), linked in the package’s CRAN DESCRIPTION
rules.requirement: Use version control and link it in the package CRAN DESCRIPTION.

rules.quote: you cannot expect all readers to be familiar with the jargon in your field.
rules.requirement: Explain field-specific jargon for a broad R audience.
